meta.title: Requirements — Bathtub Wastewater Overflow Trip Lever
meta.provenance_note: Each requirement is a restatement of a statement in the project brief, or of a rule published by the official body that regulates the work (CSLB, San Francisco DBI, California statute, California Plumbing Code). Owner-stated requirements cite the data file; code-derived requirements cite the official page. No requirement is inferred beyond those two sources.

requirements.requirement: Bathtub wastewater overflow trip lever is stuck inside the hidden plumbing behind the wall and must be removed/repaired.
The overflow is in a hard-to-access area; opening drywall to reach the plumbing is a possible but non-preferred outcome.
5+ licensed plumbers have already been unable to remove it from above without concern over destroying the hidden plumbing behind the wall.
Removal from above is the preferred outcome if a provider can perform it safely.
If above-access is not possible, the accepted approach recommended by consulted plumbers is working from below.
The space below is a storage unit; below-floor work may require opening the drywall ceiling to access the hidden plumbing.
A single coordinated service must perform both the plumbing work and the drywall (ceiling) opening and restoration — one accountable vendor for both trades.
The vendor must be a licensed plumber or contractor.
The vendor must service San Francisco.
Vendor must have experience doing delicate work in a sensitive environment: the unit is tenant-occupied.
Candidate vendors must be surfaced from review-backed services (e.g., Yelp and similar review platforms) for this specific type of work.
Reference photos of the work area may be supplied later; until then, planning proceeds from the written description only.
Collect, organize, and analyze the full requirements list plus the three received estimates into a reviewable dashboard with per-row source links.
Every published data row must carry a source link; values that cannot be confirmed from an official source are left blank and flagged as unverified — never inferred.

Any entry into the tenant-occupied unit for the repair must follow California Civil Code §1954: reasonable written notice stating date, approximate time and purpose; 24 hours is presumed reasonable; normal business hours unless the tenant consents at the time.

Any concealed slip-joint connection reached through a ceiling opening must be left with an accessible opening of the size the Plumbing Code requires (12 in. × 12 in. in the 2022 CPC §402.10; §404.2 in the 2010 edition) — a solid patch without an access panel does not meet the code.
requirements.source: California Plumbing Code §402.10 (2022) / §404.2 (2010) via IAPMO and UpCodes

requirements.requirement: San Francisco DBI states a permit is required before cutting into or replacing pipes, particularly pipes that will be covered by a wall; exemptions are listed in SF Plumbing Code §104.2. The licensed contractor applies for it (A, B, C-4/C-36, C-16, C-20 or C-54 licences may apply).
requirements.source: SF.gov / DBI — Apply for a plumbing and mechanical permit

requirements.requirement: The contract structure must be legal under B&P §7057: either one B (or B+C-36) licensee as prime for plumbing plus the second unrelated trade (drywall), or a C-36 plumber as prime with a licensed drywall contractor subcontracted. A C-36 licensee alone may not contract for drywall.
requirements.source: CSLB — B General Building classification page quoting B&P §7057

requirements.requirement: Before signing, confirm on the CSLB record that the licence is current and active, that the classification matches the work, and check the contractor's bond and workers'-compensation entry (three candidates in this set are workers'-comp exempt, meaning they certify no employees).
requirements.source: CSLB licence-detail records linked per provider

requirements.requirement: Every candidate must give a written, itemised scope and price covering: making good the trip lever, the ceiling opening, framing, the access panel, patching/texture/paint, protection of the tenant's belongings, and debris removal — one document, one accountable party.
